title: Traffic conditioning and LTS promoter: region-aware rollout gates for hosted-api
creator: Sofia Almeida
description:
Goal: Harden the Hosted API deployment pipeline with a region-aware 'LTS promoter' and traffic conditioning gates so upgrades can be staged by release channel and geography with deterministic rollback/hold behavior. This ticket implements the control plane and runtime hooks needed for: (1) pinning customers to LTS channels, (2) promoting a version through canary->regional->global stages, and (3) automated traffic throttling/conditioning when SLOs deviate.

Why this work: we saw two incidents last year where global swaps caused transient token-price spikes and cache stampedes during rollouts. Existing blue/green flow lacks region-specific holdpoints and fine-grained, SLO-driven weight modulation. The LTS promoter will let product teams declare a version as 'lts-stable' and create a promoter policy that sequences traffic shifts by region with enforced telemetry checks.

Scope and deliverables:
- Control-plane: new 'promote-release' operation that accepts: version, channel (lts/beta), region ordering, and an ordered list of gates (latency, 5xx rate, token-cost drift).
- Runtime hooks: traffic conditioning library to apply gradual weight ramps (min step 2%/30s), automated momentum smoothing, and deterministic fallback to previous LTS variant.
- Gate engine: SLO rule evaluator that reads from Console thresholds (per-route SLOs) and produces PASS/HOLD/FAIL; integrates with telemetry (Grafana/Prometheus) and traces (Honeycomb).
- KV/cache strategy: coordinated KV cache invalidation/priming strategy to prevent thundering herd when a region switches variants.
- Ops UX: Console rollout UI updates and a promote-release CLI that can simulate a rollout and produce a preflight report.
- Safety artifacts: runbook, rollback matrix, postmortem checklist, and a small canary-only chaos test harness.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Weight ramp granularity: choose 2% steps every 30s vs 5%/60s. Rationale: finer steps reduce request-level shock but increase rollout duration. We chose 2%/30s for hosted-api (configurable per-customer).
- Gate evaluation window: 90s sliding window (p99 latency, 1m error-rate). Trade-off: shorter window reduces time to detect regressions but increases noise. We will bias toward 90s with noise suppression (EWMA) and require sustained violation for 2 consecutive windows to FAIL.
- LTS pinning semantics: customers on LTS channel are pinned to last-promoted LTS variant. Pin change requires explicit promoter action or can be auto-rolled after a configurable stabilization period. This avoids surprise drift for enterprise users.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before rollout scheduler is enabled):
1) promote-release control-plane API implemented and documented in Confluence (link below).
2) Gate engine can evaluate SLOs and return PASS/HOLD/FAIL against synthetic and live telemetry.
3) End-to-end test: simulated rollout in staging moves traffic in region-order with expected ramp steps and rolls back automatically when gate FAILs.
4) KV priming strategy prevents >5x cache-miss spike on rollout in staging.
5) Console shows rollout plan, current weights, gate status, and allows operator override (with audit log).
6) Runbook and tech-contact are published; automated alert routing created in PagerDuty.

Implementation notes and checklist:
- Control plane changes: add /releases/promote endpoint in release-service (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-service/pull/804).
- Gate evaluator: new service release-gates (K8s deployment) reading metrics from Prometheus and traces from Honeycomb (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-gates/pull/12).
- Runtime client: extend traffic-proxy with TrafficConditioner v2 (library) to accept ramp profiles and safe-eviction hooks. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-proxy/pull/256.
- KV strategy: implement 'staggered-prime' for Redis clusters in region prior to switch; small sidecar will do progressive priming (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-primer/pull/7).
- Console: rollout UI wireframes and API calls documented in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Promote+Release+Spec). UI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/331.
- CLI: add 'rwd promote' dry-run mode first; follow with commit mode. CLI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/129.

Staging plan and tests:
- Stage in alpha region (us-west-2) with synthetic load that mirrors production mix.
- Run synthetic canary for 2h with deliberate latency perturbations to validate HOLD/FAIL.
- Chaos: short 1m network flaps to validate fallback behavior.
- Validate cache-miss curves vs baseline and check token-cost drift < 3%.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: gating thresholds too aggressive leading to blocked rollouts. Mitigation: provide 'override' for on-call with two-person approval and explicit audit trail.
- Risk: oversmoothing hides regressions. Mitigation: add anomaly detection that can short-circuit smoothing when a sharp spike exceeds emergency thresholds.
- Risk: cross-region dependencies (shared backing services) cause correlated failures. Mitigation: preflight include smoke calls to dependent services and mark a region as NO-GO if dependencies fail.

- 2026-03-12 Marcus Chen: TrafficConditioner v2 implemented in traffic-proxy branch feature/traffic-conditioner; unit tests added.
- 2026-03-13 QA: Began staging runbook validation; observed a cache-miss spike in first trial -> adjusted KV priming to prefetch top 5% hot keys.

Open questions (needs PM/SRE alignment):
- Default ramp config per plan (free/prod/enterprise) and maximum rollout duration SLA for customer-facing LTS promotions.
- Whether promote-release should be multi-tenant (single global operation affecting many customers) or per-tenant (queue per-tenant to limit blast radius). Current plan: per-tenant as default with optional global mode for infra teams.

acceptance_tests:
1) run `rwd promote --dry-run` against staging and confirm the preflight report lists no NO-GO issues.
2) kick off end-to-end simulated rollout and assert rollbacks trigger on gate FAIL and that console shows historical weight changes.
3) confirm no >5x cache-miss spike and 95% of hotkeys primed before 1st weight step.
4) confirm audit-log entries for every override and promotion event.
